items.title: Bill Crow interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: And Benny Powell was in the trombone section

ctx.x: Is this about the time you mentioned you saw the Basie band come in to Birdland?

Oh that was earlier. You know I became a denizen of Birdland as soon as I got to town. That was the one place that was available to me. That’s why I rented that first room a block away on 8th Avenue. I’d go down there every night because I didn’t have much of anyplace else to go. And I think the admission was less than a dollar then. And you could go down and sit in the bleachers and you didn’t have to spend another nickel, and listen to Charlie Parker, you know? He was there with his own band for the first two…

featured them on a number called “Two Franks.” And Benny Powell was in the trombone section, Wendell Cully I think. Thad Jones hadn’t come on the band yet I think. I can’t remember now whether Joe Wilder was there or not. But I know there was a lot of changing around that went on from time to time in the band.

items.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 16, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Well for example Bill Crow, I don’t know if you know him he’s a bass player.

ctx.x: Yeah. It can become consuming when you get involved in something.
Well for example Bill Crow, I don’t know if you know him he’s a bass player.
